I'm an experienced Research/HPC Engineer with a background in mathematical modelling and applied statistics.

I work at the [Natural History Museum](https://www.nhm.ac.uk) as a research engineer in the [Biodiversity Futures Lab](https://www.nhm.ac.uk/our-science/research/projects/predicts.html) on the [Biodiversity Intactness Index (BII)](https://www.nhm.ac.uk/our-science/services/data/biodiversity-intactness-index.html). I lead the software engineering behind the BII, which involves developing and publishing R packages, lots of refactoring and optimisation (!), and a lot of HPC work to build a reproducible data pipeline to generate global biodiversity data.

I completed a PhD in applied maths at [the University of Western Australia](https://www.uwa.edu.au/) in 2022, and was a postdoc at [the University of Cambridge](https://www.cam.ac.uk/) from 2021-2024. I worked in-between scientific machine learning and applied mathematics, developing numerical methods to assimilate observations into physical models.

My undergrad degree was in Mathematics and Statistics, which I also completed at the [University of Western Australia](https://www.uwa.edu.au/) in 2018. In my honours thesis I worked on modelling daily rainfall across Australia using [mixture models](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mixture_model).

## Selected Software

- [**predictsr**](https://github.com/Biodiversity-Futures-Lab/predictsr): an R package to load the [PREDICTS](https://www.nhm.ac.uk/our-science/research/projects/predicts.html) database into R dataframes and cache them to disk. Published on [CRAN](https://cran.r-project.org/package=predictsr).
- [**ssmooth**](https://github.com/Biodiversity-Futures-Lab/ssmooth): an R package for smoothing spatial data using statistical methods. Published on [CRAN](https://cran.r-project.org/package=ssmooth).
